issue.title: YOLO mode: mid-stream socket close is not retried, making large code generation impossible
issue.body:
## What happened?

In YOLO mode (`--yolo` / `-p` headless), generating large code output
(500+ lines, e.g. a complete HTML game) consistently fails with:

[API Error: terminated (cause: UND_ERR_SOCKET: other side closed)]

The DashScope gateway closes the TCP connection after ~3-5 minutes of
SSE streaming. This is 100% reproducible (5/5 attempts).

## Root cause analysis

The OpenAI SDK's stream-transport retry is gated on `!streamYieldedChunk`.
Once thinking/reasoning chunks have started flowing (which happens within
seconds for thinking models), a mid-stream socket close does NOT trigger
retry — it throws directly.

YOLO mode compounds this: the entire think → tool → think → tool loop
runs as a single uninterrupted SSE stream (3-5 min), while interactive
plan mode breaks it into independent short requests (each <30s) that
never hit the gateway timeout.

## Evidence

| Test | Result |
|------|--------|
| YOLO + large generation (5 attempts) | ❌ All fail with UND_ERR_SOCKET |
| Plan mode + same prompt | ✅ Works |
| Python httpx + same API + same model | ✅ Works (7+ min stream) |
| Modified undici keepAliveTimeout 60s→600s | ❌ Still fails |
| Small tasks in YOLO (<100 lines) | ✅ Works |

## Expected behavior

Mid-stream socket closes should be retried (at least once) even after
chunks have been yielded, similar to how connection-level errors are
retried. The `!streamYieldedChunk` gate is too conservative for
thinking models that produce long streams.

## Suggested fix

1. In `classifyRetryError`, classify `UND_ERR_SOCKET` as
   `{kind:'transport', diagnosis:'retryable'}` regardless of
   `streamYieldedChunk` state
2. On retry, send the accumulated partial output as context so the
   model can continue from where it left off
3. Alternatively: in YOLO mode, automatically break long generations
   into multi-turn (plan → execute → verify) instead of one stream

## Environment

- Qwen Code: v0.21.0
- Node.js: v22.13.1
- OS: Windows 10
- Model: qwen3.8-max-preview (thinking model)
- API: DashScope Token Plan (token-plan.cn-beijing.maas.aliyuncs.com)

  isRetryableStreamTransportError &&

[OpenCode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) - [Qwen Code](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code) - [Claude Code Skills](https://github.com/anthropics/skills) --- ## 横向对比 基于您提供的 2026 年 7 月 28 日各主流 AI CLI 工具社区动态，以下为您定制的横向对比分析报告： ### 1. 生态全景 当前 AI CLI 工具正全面迈向**多代理编排与复杂工作流自动化**阶段，底层架构调整频繁。随着工具自主权的扩大，**长上下文处理与资源（内存/磁盘）管理**成为各大工具普遍遭遇的工程瓶颈。同时，**跨平台（特别是 Windows 环境）兼容性**与**外部工具集成（如 MCP 协议）的安全性、稳定性**是决定开发者体验的关键分水岭。整体而言，AI CLI 正在从“代码生成助手”演变为“重度自动化 Agent”，随之而来的底层权限管控与系统级稳定性挑战日益凸显。 ### 2. 各工具活跃度对比 以下为今日各核心工具的社区基础活跃度指标： | 工具名称 | 今日 Release | 热度 Top Issues | 重要 PR 进展 | 核心动态标签 | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Claude Code** | 0 | 10 | 7 | 计费异常、提示词干预争议、Windows痛点 | | **OpenAI Codex** | 2 (Alpha) | 10 | N/A (未披露) | 高频迭代、Windows崩溃、磁盘泄漏 | | **Gemini CLI** | 1 (Nightly)| 10 | 10 | 子代理稳定性、AST感知、隐私脱敏 | | **GitHub Copilot CLI**| 1 | 8 | N/A (已修复多项) | 性能优化、会话损坏、UI渲染异常 | | **Kimi Code CLI** | 0 | 4 | 4 | 本地化编码修复、IDE插件稳定性 | | **OpenCode** | 2 | 10 | 9 | 桌面端重构、插件热重载、复杂工作流 | | **Qwen Code** | 1 (Nightly)| 10 | 9 | 高危安全漏洞、沙箱逃逸、长上下文断连 | ### 3. 共同关注的功能方向 * **Windows 及跨平台兼容性**：几乎所有工具都在与 Windows 环境的底层机制“搏斗”。*Claude Code* 面临虚拟机文件系统错误（ENOENT）和终端卡死；*Codex* 遭遇嵌入式浏览器内存越界崩溃；*Copilot CLI* 出现 UI 渲染消失；而 *Kimi Code* 和 *Gemini CLI* 则在全力修复中文 GBK 编码导致的 Unicode 崩溃及换行符差异问题。 * **上下文压缩与资源（OOM）泄漏**：长会话导致的内存/磁盘暴增成为通病。*Codex* 会话日志激增至 2GB，子代理引发疯狂磁盘占用；*Gemini CLI* 遭遇千级文件 OOM；*Copilot CLI* 刚修复了 5MB issue.title: fix(core): retry mid-stream transport failures as continuations

repository.name: qwen-code
repository.description: An open-source AI coding agent that lives in your terminal.

issue.body:
## What this PR does

Fixes #7832. The stream transport retry used to fire only before the first chunk reached callers, so a socket close anywhere into a long thinking stream (UND_ERR_SOCKET minutes in) propagated and threw away everything already generated. With this change, when chunks have already flowed and the failed attempt left a text or thought partial, the retry runs as a continuation instead: the partial turn stays in history, a recovery user message shows the model its own suffix, and the model picks up where the stream died. One continuation per send; if it fails, the partial turn survives in history and on the transcript, and the error propagates as before.

## Why it's needed

YOLO/headless generation of large outputs fails consistently for thinking models today: the whole think -> tool loop runs as a single SSE stream that outlives the gateway's idle window, the gateway closes the socket, and the session dies with `[API Error: terminated]`. Restarting from zero would also re-print the partial output in headless mode, which is why a plain after-chunk retry was never enabled. The continuation shape reuses the same machinery as the MAX_TOKENS output recovery (recovery message, `isContinuation` retry event, coalescing), so the UI keeps its buffer and the continuation appends seamlessly in both interactive and headless modes. FunctionCall partials still propagate immediately, since a user message cannot be injected between a functionCall and its response.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

`npx vitest run src/core/geminiChat.test.ts` in `packages/core`: 242/242 pass. The new tests cover the three relevant shapes: mid-stream socket close with a text partial retries as a continuation (`RETRY` event with `isContinuation: true`, history coalesced to a single model turn holding partial + continuation, no synthetic user turn left behind); a functionCall partial still propagates with no retry attempt; a failed continuation keeps the partial turn and rethrows. The previously existing test that pinned "never retry after a chunk" was updated to the new contract, since that pinned behavior is exactly what #7832 reports as the bug.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A (core retry semantics, no UI surface change; the TUI's existing `isContinuation` handling keeps the text buffer, verified by reading `useGeminiStream.ts`'s Retry case).

issue.title: fix(core): resume long streams cut by a socket-level close

repository.name: qwen-code
repository.description: An open-source AI coding agent that lives in your terminal.

issue.body:
## What this PR does

Makes a response that gets cut off by a socket-level close mid-stream recoverable, instead of failing the whole send. Two changes, both in `packages/core/src/core/geminiChat.ts`.

First, the existing replay path no longer treats reasoning as delivered output. Its guard used to be "has any chunk reached the caller", which a thinking model trips within seconds of starting, so replay was unavailable for precisely the long generations that need it. The guard now asks whether anything a replay could *duplicate* was delivered — non-blank answer text or a `functionCall`. Thoughts and tool-call preparation metadata no longer count. This is consistent with the rate-limit and invalid-stream branches, which already re-send after reasoning has streamed, and with the UI's non-continuation `RETRY` handler, which clears the thought buffer.

Second, once answer text *has* been delivered, replaying is genuinely off the table — the user would see the first half of the answer twice — but failing the send is not the only remaining option. The response so far is already on screen, so the fix keeps it, asks the model to resume from it, and signals the UI with `{ type: StreamEventType.RETRY, isContinuation: true }` so it appends to its text buffer rather than replacing it. This is the same shape the `MAX_TOKENS` truncation path already uses; the continuation reuses that machinery rather than introducing a parallel one. Budget is 3 attempts, since one long generation can be cut repeatedly by the same idle timeout.

Three implementation points worth a reviewer's attention. The delivered text is mirrored into a local buffer as it is yielded rather than read back from history, because it cannot be read back: `processStreamResponse` deliberately does not persist a text-only partial turn when the stream throws, so at the catch site history holds nothing about what the user already saw. The synthetic turns that carry the delivered text and the resume instruction are built into the request only and never written to `self.history`, so they cannot leak into the JSONL transcript or a later `/compress` — unlike the `MAX_TOKENS` loop, which routes through history and cleans up afterwards with `coalesceRecoveryPairs`. And on success the delivered prefix is merged back into the trailing model turn, because otherwise in-memory history would hold an answer that begins mid-sentence, which is visible on `/compress` and every later turn's context; replayed overlap is deduped with the existing `getRecoveryContinuationSuffix`. This merge targets `this.history` only, not the recorder, so the JSONL transcript that `--resume` reads still starts the turn mid-sentence -- see the Known gap below.

Cuts that delivered a `functionCall` are excluded. Injecting a user turn between a `functionCall` and its `functionResponse` produces a sequence providers reject — the same constraint the `MAX_TOKENS` recovery loop enforces through its `hasFunctionCall` check — and the scheduler's repair path already covers that case.

## Why it's needed

Long generations behind a gateway that caps SSE connection lifetime die with `TypeError: terminated` / `UND_ERR_SOCKET`, and no retry setting helps. DashScope closes at roughly 3–5 minutes, so in YOLO mode a long task is unrecoverable: the work already streamed to the screen is thrown away and the turn fails outright. Short requests never reach the timeout, so the failure is specific to exactly the requests that took the most time to produce.

A note on the two fixes suggested in #7832, since the first one is misleading. Suggested fix 1 — classify `UND_ERR_SOCKET` as retryable — is already implemented; the code is in `RETRYABLE_STREAM_TRANSPORT_CODES` in `packages/core/src/core/stream-transport-retry.ts`. The second half of that suggestion, retry regardless of whether chunks were yielded, would actively introduce a bug, because the retry in question is a replay of the whole request and the user would see duplicated output. The error classification was never the blocker; the `streamYieldedChunk` guard was. Suggested fix 2 — send the accumulated partial output as context and continue — is what this PR implements.

### How to verify

The unit suite is the primary evidence, since the production trigger needs a real gateway. From the repo root:

The behaviour is covered by a new `describe('transport stream continuation (#7832)')` block with fifteen cases: it continues from the delivered text instead of failing the send; stitches the delivered text into durable history; drops replayed overlap when the model repeats its own tail; survives repeated cuts and accumulates every delivered fragment; propagates once the continuation budget is exhausted (asserting exactly four calls — initial plus three); does not continue a cut that delivered a `functionCall`; **replays** rather than continues when only a thought was delivered; **replays** rather than continues when the delivered text was blank; and drops a pending continuation when a fresh-restart retry takes over.

## Risk & Scope

- **Main risk or tradeoff:** the one behaviour change outside the new code path is the replay guard widening, so a replay can now happen after a thought-only or blank-text prefix where it previously would not. Its downstream consumer is the non-continuation `RETRY` handler in `packages/cli/src/ui/hooks/useGeminiStream.ts`, which clears both the text and thought buffers, so a replay after a thought-only prefix renders correctly. On the continuation path the tradeoff is that the model is asked to resume from a suffix of its own output, so a model that ignores the instruction and restarts would produce a duplicated opening; the existing `getRecoveryContinuationSuffix` dedup mitigates this, and it is the same tradeoff the `MAX_TOKENS` recovery path already accepts.


## Known gap: `max_tokens` is not re-clamped for continuation attempts

Raised by @wenshao and confirmed here by reading both paths. `buildAttemptContents()` grows the prompt by the delivered text, but `params` — which carries `maxOutputTokens` — is passed to `makeApiCallAndProcessStream` unchanged, so every continuation attempt reuses the value clamped before the first send. The pre-existing `MAX_TOKENS` recovery loop re-clamps per iteration (`geminiChat.ts`, the `Re-clamp maxOutputTokens for THIS iteration` block) precisely because its prompt grows the same way:

```
transport continuation (this PR)        pre-existing MAX_TOKENS recovery
  req#0  max_tokens=32000                 req#0  max_tokens=32000
  req#1  max_tokens=32000                 req#1  max_tokens=64000   <- escalated
  req#2  max_tokens=32000                 req#2  max_tokens=64000   <- re-clamped per iteration
  req#3  max_tokens=32000
```

Neither of us can make it fail: the delivered text has to be large enough for `prompt + max_tokens` to cross the window, and the continuation budget caps the growth at three attempts. So this is a documented asymmetry with the path this PR mirrors, not a confirmed bug — recorded here rather than fixed so it is not rediscovered as a new finding. Fixing it means routing the continuation attempt through the same `clampOutputTokensToWindow` call the recovery loop uses.

## Known gap: `--resume` / `--continue`

Not fixed here, and confirmed by @wenshao with a real socket-cutting gateway. `prependTextToLastModelTurn` writes to `this.history`, not to `chatRecordingService`, so a resumed session still sees the recovered turn starting mid-sentence. `/compress` and later-turn context *are* fixed, because those read in-memory history.

The naive fix -- recording the delivered delta as its own assistant turn when the continuation is scheduled -- was prototyped and measured, and it trades this defect for a worse one: on the fresh-restart-retry path the discarded prefix is already durable, so the resumed transcript shows the answer twice. That is the exact hazard the existing comment in `processStreamResponse` warns about.

The correct fix is the stash-and-decide pattern this file already uses for `functionCall` partials (`pendingPartialAssistantRecord`): stash the delta, flush it on success alongside `prependTextToLastModelTurn`, discard it in `resetTransportContinuation`. That is a real change rather than a one-liner, so it belongs in a follow-up rather than bolted onto this PR.

Not a regression against `main`: on merge-base the cut turn records no assistant record at all.

## What

Implements the thinking-phase retry refinement scoped by @doudouOUC in https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/issues/7832#issuecomment-5090164606 (the `welcome-pr` direction): track a separate `streamYieldedContentChunk` that is only set when a chunk carries a **non-thought** candidate part (text, `functionCall`, `inlineData`, …), and gate the transport stream replay on it instead of `streamYieldedChunk`.

- New helper `hasNonThoughtCandidateParts()` next to `isToolCallPreparationOnly()` documents the invariant the gate relies on.
- The not-taken log's `retryDecision` becomes `skipped_after_content` (was `skipped_after_chunk`; single producer, no other consumers — verified by grep), and the retry-scheduled log gains `yieldedNonContentChunks` so thinking-phase replays are visible in diagnostics.
- Content-phase behavior is unchanged: once any non-thought part has flowed, the replay stays blocked and the error propagates.

## Why

`streamYieldedChunk` trips on the first thinking chunk — within seconds for thinking models — while the model can then spend minutes reasoning. That is exactly when gateways close long-lived SSE connections (`UND_ERR_SOCKET`, reporter's 5/5 repro; same server-side cause as #7831). The retry was already classified as safe (`UND_ERR_SOCKET` ∈ `RETRYABLE_STREAM_TRANSPORT_CODES`) but locked out even though zero user-visible content existed.

Replaying after thinking-only output is safe because thought parts are ephemeral — they are never recorded as the assistant's final response in history (`stripThoughtPartsFromContent` and the model-parts filter drop `part.thought` before history is recorded), so a replay cannot duplicate visible output. The UI does re-render the new attempt's thinking, which is the same behavior as the existing pre-chunk retry path.

## Reviewer Test Plan

- `vitest run src/core/geminiChat.test.ts` → 262 passing. Full `src/core/` slice: 53 files / 2492 passing; `src/utils/` slice: 117 files / 4117 passing. `tsc --noEmit`, `eslint --max-warnings 0`, `prettier --check` clean.
- Existing test renamed for precision: **does not retry … after yielding a content chunk** (fixture already yields visible text).
- New: **retries a transport stream error after yielding only thinking chunks** — first attempt yields a `{ thought: true }` part then throws `UND_ERR_SOCKET`; asserts 2 API calls, exactly 1 RETRY event, and the recovered content arrives.
- New: **does not retry when visible content followed the thinking chunks** — pins that the flag accumulates across the attempt; thinking-then-content still blocks (1 API call, 0 RETRY).
- Mutation check: reverting the gate to `!streamYieldedChunk` fails exactly the thinking-retry test (1/262); neutering the content check fails exactly the two blocking tests (2/262).

Not reproduced against a live DashScope gateway: the failure needs a server-side idle close minutes into a real SSE stream. The deterministic unit tests above pin the decision logic itself; the reporter's repro matrix covers the environment side.

## Risk & Scope

One flag + one gate condition + log fields in `sendMessageStream`'s retry loop; no API or event-shape changes. The riskiest edge — a chunk with **no** parts (usage-only / finishReason-only) — now allows replay where it previously blocked; both are pre-content states where replay is safe for the same history-based reason.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #7832. Related: #7831 (same gateway idle-close, higher-context variant). The issue's suggestion (2) — partial-output continuation for content-phase failures — is explicitly out of scope per the triage discussion; it needs API-level continuation semantics and a design doc.

Refs: #8094

## The bug

After a socket cut mid-response, the transport-continuation path asks the model to resume from the text the user already saw. On success, `prependTextToLastModelTurn` merges that delivered prefix back into the trailing model turn — but it writes `this.history` and nothing else:

https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/main/packages/core/src/core/geminiChat.ts#L2731-L2733

So `/compress` and every later turn read a coherent answer, while the JSONL transcript that `--resume` / `--continue` reads keeps only the resumed remainder. The recovered turn starts mid-sentence on resume.

Not a regression: before #7896 the cut turn recorded no assistant record at all.

## The fix

Merge the prefix into the assistant record as it is built, reusing the same overlap dedup `prependTextToLastModelTurn` already uses. One turn in, one matching turn on disk.

**Why at the record build and not next to the history merge.** The record is appended from inside `processStreamResponse`, before the outer send loop regains control at `:2731`, and `appendRecord` is append-only. A second record written "alongside `prependTextToLastModelTurn`" would land *after* the remainder, and resume maps records to `Content[]` in file order — so the transcript would read `[remainder][prefix]`, halves reversed. That rules out the record-a-second-turn shape.

**Why success-only.** On `streamError !== null` the record must keep matching the remainder-only partial that survives in history (the `pendingPartialAssistantRecord` path), and a fresh-restart retry discards the prefix from history via `resetTransportContinuation`. Merging unconditionally would put the delivered text in the transcript but not in history — the same desync, pointing the other way.

**Why a parameter, not a field.** The prefix rides as a per-attempt argument captured by value, so it dies with the attempt. There is no stash that can dangle into a later turn — which matters, because `NO_TOOL_RESULT_PROGRESS_MAX_TOKENS` breaks out of the loop without reaching either the merge or the reset, and an instance-field stash flushed in the generator's `finally` would write a spurious prefix record there.

`resetTransportContinuation` needs no change: it already clears `transportContinuationPrefix`, so the next attempt is invoked with `undefined`.

## Proof

`packages/core`, Node 22.22.3, fully mocked (fake timers, no network).

**RED** — new tests against unmodified `geminiChat.ts`:

```
FAIL > transport stream continuation (#7832) > records the delivered prefix with the resumed remainder in one turn
  expected 'second half' to be 'first half second half'

FAIL > transport stream continuation (#7832) > dedupes replayed overlap in the recorded turn too
  expected 'jumps over the lazy dog.' to be 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.'

Tests  2 failed | 16 passed | 285 skipped (303)
```

The two guard tests (discard-on-reset, and the tool-call-cut case) pass on unmodified source — they are tripwires, not the red.

**GREEN**

```
Tests  19 passed | 285 skipped (304)     # transport stream continuation block
```

**Mutation checks** — each mutant killed by exactly the test that should catch it:

| Mutant | Result |
|---|---|
| drop `streamError === null &&` (merge on failure too) | FAIL `keeps the record remainder-only when the continuation itself is cut after a tool call` |
| `prefix + contentText` (naive concat, no overlap dedup) | FAIL `dedupes replayed overlap in the recorded turn too` |
| never thread the prefix (pass `undefined`) | FAIL both merge tests |

**Blast radius**, by symbol not directory. `processStreamResponse` has one production caller plus a direct call in `goal-turn-integration.test.ts`; `makeApiCallAndProcessStream` has three call sites (`:2696` changed, `:3225` and `:3899` pass nothing → `undefined` → byte-identical behavior). Every file matching those symbols or `recordAssistantTurn`:

```
✓ src/core/geminiChat.test.ts                       (304 tests)
✓ src/core/client.test.ts                           (316 tests)
✓ src/services/chatRecordingService.test.ts          (69 tests)
✓ src/services/chatRecordingService.autoTitle.test.ts (20 tests)
✓ src/core/goal-turn-integration.test.ts              (3 tests)
```

**Full suite, against restored upstream sources vs this branch:**

```
upstream main   19235 passed | 11 skipped | 0 failed
this branch     19239 passed | 11 skipped | 0 failed    (+4, the new tests)
```

`tsc --noEmit` exit 0 on both.

## Demo

N/A — no user-facing change in the live session. The change is to the durable transcript, and the observable difference is the recorded turn text, asserted directly in the tests above.

## Limits

- Proof drives the real `sendMessageStream` → `processStreamResponse` path with a stubbed content generator; it does not run against a gateway that really destroys the TCP socket. The original measurements in #8094 are @wenshao's from that setup.
- Pre-existing and left alone: when a continuation fails unretryably, the delivered text is in neither history nor the transcript. Both layers agree, so it is not this bug, but it is still text the user saw and no layer keeps.

issue.body:
## What this PR does

Models that legitimately end a turn silently right after a tool result — valid `finish_reason`, no visible text, no further tool call — currently trip the `NO_TOOL_RESULT_PROGRESS` guard in `GeminiChat.processStreamResponse`, burn the four-retry invalid-stream budget on identical responses, and then abort the entire run with `[API Error: Model stream ended after a tool result without visible progress.]`. This PR keeps the retry-first behavior from #7039 and changes only what happens once that budget is exhausted: the final attempt accepts the quiet completion as a legitimate turn end instead of re-throwing. The `NO_TOOL_RESULT_PROGRESS_MAX_TOKENS` variant stays fatal (a truncated turn is genuinely incomplete), and ordinary mid-retry semantics are untouched — models that only occasionally go quiet still get their four chances to produce progress. When the accepted turn produced nothing at all, the canonical `(empty content)` placeholder becomes the turn's text: it keeps user/model alternation well-formed for the next request, is already filtered out of tool-result continuation rendering, and rides into the JSONL record through the same `contentText` the history push derives from, so transcript and history stay in agreement.

## Why it's needed

The reporter ran ~390 automated headless rollouts on the same tasks and harness, varying only the model: 291 GPT-family and 96 Gemini-family runs failed with this exact error (the dominant failure mode), while 0 Qwen runs hit it — Qwen models always emit content after a tool result, GPT/Gemini-family models can legitimately end the turn quietly. Because the run is headless, there is no interactive retry; the whole run is lost. Two independent source traces in the issue thread (triage + a maintainer confirmation on current `main`) pin the mechanism to the throw site in `geminiChat.ts`, and the issue was already confirmed and scoped: accept the quiet completion after retry exhaustion, keep the `MAX_TOKENS` variant failing.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. `cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/core/geminiChat.test.ts` — 318/318 pass, including:
   - `should accept a thought-only tool result continuation once the retry budget is exhausted (#9026)` — the model goes thought-only after the tool result on every attempt; the stream still makes 5 attempts (1 + 4 retries, `logContentRetry` ×4, RETRY events present) and then COMPLETES instead of rejecting, with the thought turn surviving in history. Verified red-before/green-after: with the source change stashed, the two new tests fail.
   - `should accept a fully quiet tool result completion after retry exhaustion and keep history well-formed (#9026)` — every attempt is a bare `STOP` with zero parts; after the budget is spent the stream completes, history ends on a `model` turn carrying `(empty content)` (never on the user's `functionResponse`), and `recordAssistantTurn` receives the same placeholder text.
2. Pre-existing protections remain pinned: the #7039 retry tests (`should retry semantically empty responses after a tool result`, `should not retry tool result continuations that make another tool call`) and the `MAX_TOKENS` escalation tests all pass unchanged.
3. `npm run typecheck` in `packages/core`: clean. ESLint and Prettier on both changed files: clean. Full `packages/core` suite: no new failures versus the clean-baseline run (both runs share the same ~60 pre-existing environment-dependent failures in logger/fs/provider-preset areas; 0 geminiChat failures either way).

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — core stream-validation change with no TUI surface; covered by the unit evidence above.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ not tested |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅ tested |

### Environment (optional)

Vitest with fake timers against the mocked content generator (same harness as the #7039 tests); no live model calls.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a genuinely glitched empty continuation now ends the turn quietly after the retries are spent, where it previously surfaced as a loud error. Mitigation: the retry budget is fully preserved first (five identical attempts), the acceptance is a per-attempt one-shot flag captured and cleared inside `processStreamResponse` (it cannot leak to an unrelated later send), the `MAX_TOKENS` truncation variant stays fatal, and the accepted turn leaves a well-formed placeholder model turn plus a matching JSONL record rather than a dangling `user[functionResponse]` tail.
- Not validated / out of scope: live OpenRouter reproduction (needs external model access); the related subagent paths #7835/#7126 and IDEA-plugin symptom #4888 named in the issue's related list are separate surfaces; the reporter's suggestion of an interactive-mode recovery path is out of scope here.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. Behavior change is limited to post-tool-result streams that exhaust the invalid-stream retry budget with no visible progress — previously a hard failure, now a clean completion.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #9026

## 这个 PR 做了什么

在工具结果之后合法地静默结束回合的模型（有效 `finish_reason`、无可见文本、无后续工具调用）目前会触发 `GeminiChat.processStreamResponse` 中的 `NO_TOOL_RESULT_PROGRESS` 守卫，在四次相同的无效重重试后以 `[API Error: Model stream ended after a tool result without visible progress.]` 中止整个运行。本 PR 保留 #7039 的"先重试"行为，只改变预算耗尽后的结果：最后一次尝试把静默完成接受为合法的回合结束，而不是再次抛错。`NO_TOOL_RESULT_PROGRESS_MAX_TOKENS` 变体仍然报错（被截断的回合确实不完整），中途重试语义不变——只是偶尔静默的模型依然有四次产生进展的机会。当被接受的回合完全没有产出时，用规范的 `(empty content)` 占位符作为该回合文本：保证下一次请求时 user/model 交替结构完整、已被工具结果续接渲染过滤、并且经由与 history push 相同来源的 `contentText` 写入 JSONL 记录，转录与历史保持一致。

   - `should accept a fully quiet tool result completion after retry exhaustion and keep history well-formed (#9026)`——每次尝试都是零 part 的裸 `STOP`；预算耗尽后流完成，历史以带 `(empty content)` 的 `model` 回合结尾（不会停在 user 的 `functionResponse` 上），`recordAssistantTurn` 收到相同占位文本。
2. 既有保护仍被固化：#7039 的重试测试（`should retry semantically empty responses after a tool result`、`should not retry tool result continuations that make another tool call`）与 `MAX_TOKENS` 升级测试全部原样通过。
3. `packages/core` 下 `npm run typecheck`：干净。两个改动文件的 ESLint 与 Prettier：干净。`packages/core` 全量套件：相对干净基线无新增失败（两次运行共享同一批约 60 个 logger/fs/provider-preset 环境预存失败；geminiChat 两边都是 0 失败）。

### 环境（可选）

对 mock content generator 使用 vitest 假定时器（与 #7039 测试同一 harness）；无真实模型调用。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或权衡：真正出错的空续接在重试耗尽后会静默结束回合，而之前会以显眼的错误暴露。缓解：先完整保留重试预算（五次相同尝试）；接受逻辑是每次尝试一次性标志，在 `processStreamResponse` 内捕获并清除，不会泄漏到无关的后续发送；`MAX_TOKENS` 截断变体仍然报错；被接受的回合留下结构完整的占位 model 回合与匹配的 JSONL 记录，而不是悬空的 `user[functionResponse]` 结尾。

issue.body:
## What this PR does

Loop detection missed verbatim repetition when the repeated unit was longer than about 75 characters, on both the visible-content channel and the reasoning/thinking channel. This PR adds a long-period repetition rule to the content chunk analysis and routes thought text into the content-repetition detectors, so a multi-sentence block chanted verbatim now halts the turn.

## Why it's needed

Issue #1775 reports the model chanting one ~300-char analysis block ("The issue might be that the API call is not being made properly when the switch is toggled. Let me make sure the fetchPublicRecipes function is called correctly...") over and over without the turn ever halting; a follow-up comment reports the same symptom in the thinking stream with a ~540-char block. Two gaps combine: the chunk-hash rule only admits repeat units up to ~75 chars (occurrences must cluster within `1.5 * CONTENT_CHUNK_SIZE`), and reasoning streamed as thought parts never reaches the content detectors at all (`getResponseText` filters `thought` parts out of `Content` events). This is related to #9656 but not covered by #9660, whose own tests note the repeated unit must still fit the 75-char cluster window.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the loop detection unit tests: `cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/services/loopDetectionService.test.ts`. The new `Long verbatim repetition loops (issue #1775)` describe block streams the exact repeated block from the report as misaligned deltas (so no two adjacent deltas are identical, like real token streaming) through `LoopDetectionService.addAndCheck` and asserts detection on both channels, plus negative cases: varied reasoning must not halt, equal-stride occurrences with varying intervening text must not halt, and four repetitions (below the five-occurrence threshold) must not halt. On `main` without this fix the two positive cases fail (verified in a worktree at 04886c43); with the fix all 104 tests in the file pass, and `client.test.ts` (358 tests) is unaffected.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — detector-internal behavior, covered by the unit tests above. Before: the two positive tests fail with `expected false to be true` (no loop detected after 40 verbatim repetitions). After: they pass and `getLastLoopType()` reports `chanting_identical_sentences` at roughly the fifth repetition.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests only: `vitest run src/services/loopDetectionService.test.ts` and `src/core/client.test.ts` in `packages/core`; `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` clean for the changed files.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the new rule fires earlier than the clustered rule for genuinely periodic output (after five equally spaced occurrences and a verified periodic span of at least 1000 chars); an exact-periodicity verification keeps this to true chants, and all existing negative cases (varied content, markdown resets, code blocks, far-apart repetitions separated by varying text) still pass. The content history window grows from 1000 to 4000 chars so long units remain observable — bounded memory, indices are adjusted by the existing truncation logic.
- Not validated / out of scope: repeat units longer than roughly 950 chars exceed the retained window and rely on model/server behavior; the thought-routing piece overlaps with the open #9660 (kept textually identical for a trivial rebase whichever lands first).
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none; no public API changes.

## Linked Issues

issue.title: fix(core): retry status-less upstream errors instead of ending the turn

repository.name: qwen-code
repository.description: An open-source AI coding agent that lives in your terminal.

issue.body:
## What this PR does

Teaches the retry path to recognize an upstream failure that arrives without an HTTP status, and to recover from it instead of ending the turn. When a gateway pushes an error object into an SSE stream that already returned 200, the OpenAI SDK surfaces it with the status missing, carrying the provider's error code and message plus the request id read off the response headers. The retry classifier had no branch for that shape, so it landed in the catch-all unclassified bucket and nothing retried it.

The classifier now treats a status-less error carrying the provider's own request id as a retryable upstream failure, and fails fast on the provider codes that can never succeed on a resend — moderation, credentials/billing, malformed request — because a request id separates upstream from local, not transient from permanent. The verdict for errors an HTTP status cannot decide is computed once and shared by both establishment gates, which had each copied it.

The load-bearing half is where the error actually lands. Both establishment gates run while the stream is being set up, and the SDK builds this error inside the lazy iterator, after setup has resolved — so the mid-stream catch is the only place that ever sees it. That catch computed the classification and then ignored it: its only retry exits required a socket code. It now admits this class to both existing recovery mechanisms beside the transport one, under a predicate of its own — replay when nothing user-visible has been delivered, continuation from the delivered text once it has — reusing their budgets and every no-duplication precondition. The socket allow-list is deliberately untouched, because the Anthropic generator shares it to decide whether deferred tool-call chunks may be released.

Widening that gate exposed an ordering fault of its own, fixed in the third round: the gate is consulted before the one-shot overflow recovery below it, so a status-less input-length rejection was re-sent instead of compacted, and the continuation arm re-sent it strictly larger on each attempt. Both overflow detectors are now computed above the gate and their hits excluded from the widened verdict — from that verdict only, so a socket cut keeps the verdict it had before this branch existed. Permanence is also read off the provider's `.type` field and not only its `code`, because the OpenAI SDK puts `invalid_request_error` on `.type` with `code` null. And the three stream-recovery logs now carry the classification's reason, provider code and request id, without which the class this PR recovers could not be triaged from its own logs.

## Why it's needed

A turn that had been running for over four hours was ended instantly by a server-side defect in the model gateway: 43 seconds into a streaming request the upstream returned `code: 'KeyError'` with `message: "'id'"` and no HTTP status. The same session absorbed dozens of socket drops without a hiccup, because those classify as transport errors and get retried; this shape was not retried at all. That asymmetry is the bug — a transient server-side failure the provider itself traced with a request id is at least as retryable as a socket cut, yet it was the one status-less shape that got no retry. The user-visible cost is total: the turn aborts, the failure surfaces as the two characters `'id'` with no context, and everything in flight is lost. It reproduced three times in eleven hours on the same model.

The first commit of this PR did not actually fix that. It taught the classifier the shape and widened both establishment gates, and review measured that neither gate ever sees the error: `pipeline.executeStream` awaits only the response creation and returns an unstarted generator, so the retried call resolves before a single SSE frame is parsed. The second commit moves the decision to the mid-stream catch, where the error really arrives. The establishment gates remain, but they are belt-and-braces for this class — no producer in the installed SDK builds it before iteration.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Confirm these behaviors:

1. A streaming request whose upstream pushes an error frame mid-stream, with no HTTP status, is replayed on the same model when nothing user-visible has been delivered yet, and the turn completes when a later attempt succeeds. Expect a retry event and a second call to the generator.
2. The same failure after answer text has already reached the caller continues from that text instead of replaying — the caller keeps what is on screen, the model is asked to resume, and both halves arrive exactly once. This is the same recovery a socket cut gets.
3. A permanent provider rejection delivered the same way — a moderation code such as `data_inspection_failed`, a credential or billing code, a malformed-request code — still propagates on the first attempt: one call, no retry event. Re-sending the identical request can never succeed, and the production ladder costs about eighty seconds to walk.
4. Permanent local failures are unchanged. A missing API key, an invalid MCP server configuration, and MCP protocol errors (numeric JSON-RPC codes) all still fail on the first attempt — none carries an upstream request id. An empty request id does not open the gate either: `x-request-id` can be present and empty, which is what a proxy emits when the upstream set none.
5. An upstream error that does carry an HTTP status keeps its existing verdict: a traced 400 still fails fast, a 5xx still retries, 429/503 still take the rate-limit path. A socket cut that is also traced with a request id stays transport-classified, so replay, continuation and the Anthropic deferred-tool-call release all keep working.
6. Nothing unbounded was unlocked. A status-less upstream error does not enter persistent retry mode (still requires a 429 or 529 status), does not trigger model fallback (still requires a status), and its mid-stream recovery is bounded by the existing budgets — two replays, three continuations.
7. An oversized-payload rejection delivered the same way — status-less, traced, carrying a code the permanence list does not know — reaches the one-shot compaction instead of being replayed: a COMPRESSED event first, then the retry, then the compacted answer. Re-sending cannot shrink a request, so the recovery gate must not adopt it.
8. A malformed-request rejection that carries its permanence on the provider's `.type` rather than its `code` fails fast, while a `.type` of `server_error` on the same shape stays retryable.

The real-world failure this fixes, as recorded by the daemon and the session transcript:

```
qwen-code.api_error  error_type="APIError"  error_message="'id'"  status_code=(absent)
                     response_id=cd7f37f3-d38a-9dec-804f-f70dda5650eb  duration_ms=42925
turn_result          state="error"  error={"message":"'id'","code":"KeyError"}
prompt turn failed: [code -32603] 'id'
```

The bare-UUID response id is the tell: successful completions on that model report `chatcmpl-<uuid>`, so the id came from the error's own request-id field, not from a completion chunk.

Every test this PR adds was mutation-checked: the production change it pins was removed and the test confirmed red, then restored. Removing the mid-stream disjunct turns both mid-stream tests red with the incident's own `'id'`; removing the permanent-code list turns three red, including the propagation test reporting a second generator call instead of hanging; reverting the empty-id normalization and the request-id branch each turn their own cases red. The third round's additions were checked the same way: dropping the overflow exclusion gives `expected 'retry' to be 'compressed'`, dropping the `.type` term reds the malformed-request case while widening it to "any type is permanent" reds the `server_error` guard, deleting one code from the permanence list reds the code sweep, removing `requestID` from the reader reds the real-SDK oracle, and removing `requestId` from the recovery log reds the log assertion.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — no UI or TUI surface changes. The observable difference is that a turn survives a mid-stream gateway error instead of aborting; the production log excerpt above is the Before, and the mid-stream tests are the After.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests only, on macOS: full workspace build, full typecheck, formatting and lint on the changed files, and targeted runs of the retry, classification, streaming-chat, MCP client, rate-limit, OpenAI content-generator, Anthropic generator, both non-streaming LLM clients and chat-compression suites — 2495 tests green. No live provider was used; the upstream shape was taken from a recorded session and cross-checked against the installed SDK's stream iterator.

A full `packages/core` run was also compared against the same suite at the parent commit. Both runs carry environment failures on this machine (real-git, filesystem and hook-timeout cases); the parent's failing set is a strict subset of the local one, the four failures in files this PR touches are hook and test timeouts rather than assertion mismatches, and each of those files passes in isolation on this tree.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: an upstream rejection that is genuinely permanent but arrives without a status and without a code this PR recognizes now costs bounded recovery attempts before failing, where it previously failed immediately — two replays or three continuations mid-stream, up to seven attempts on the establishment paths. The known permanent classes are now fail-fasted on their provider code, and allocated-quota and Qwen OAuth quota were already fail-fasted ahead of this branch.
- Second tradeoff: the discriminator is a request id, which proves the provider traced the failure but not that the failure is transient. A deny-list of permanent provider codes is the counterweight, and it is a list — a provider that invents a new permanent code will have it retried until someone adds it. The alternative, an allow-list of transient codes, was rejected because it would reintroduce the original bug for the next unexpected gateway fault.
- Two known residuals, both under-inclusion rather than regression. A mid-stream frame whose *body* carries a numeric code (`{"code":500}`) derives a status from that body, so it classifies as a wire 5xx and the mid-stream gates decline it while the establishment gates retry it; this is byte-identical at the merge base, and closing it needs a marker recording that a status came from the body rather than the wire — a change to the classification contract that also has to avoid stacking the stream budget on top of the rate-limit budget. Separately, the establishment-path verdict does not consult the overflow detectors, so a status-less oversized-payload rejection whose code is not in the permanence list is still retried on the drain-inside-the-call path; the canonical `context_length_exceeded` is in that list, and wiring compaction heuristics into the shared classifier would couple retry classification to compaction policy.
- Not validated / out of scope: no integration test drives a fake OpenAI SSE server emitting a mid-stream error frame, so the SDK-level shape is verified by reading the installed SDK and matching all four recorded telemetry fields rather than by an executed end-to-end repro. The under-inclusive side is also out of scope: Anthropic's mid-stream errors discard the request id entirely (its `APIError.generate` short-circuits to a connection error without headers), a gateway that omits `x-request-id` reproduces the original bug, and an id nested inside the SDK's own error body is not read. Recognizing a status-less provider-response error structurally rather than by header is a design change deserving its own PR. Also out of scope: the failure text still reaches the UI as the bare two-character message with no model or provider context.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. The classification gains two reason labels; no schema, type, or doc enumerates reason values, so they are purely additive to telemetry. Both new predicates live in modules the package barrel does not re-export.

## Linked Issues

None. Found while diagnosing an aborted session; no existing issue tracks it.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

让重试路径能识别「没有 HTTP status 的上游失败」，并从它恢复，而不是直接结束整轮。当网关把错误对象推进一个已经返回 200 的 SSE 流里时，OpenAI SDK 抛出的错误是缺 status 的，只带着服务端的错误码、错误消息，以及从响应头读到的 request id。重试分类器原本没有对应这种形状的分支，于是它落进兜底的 unclassified，没有任何环节会重试它。

现在分类器会把「无 status 但带有服务端自己的 request id」的错误判定为可重试的上游失败；同时对那些重发也绝不可能成功的服务端错误码快速失败——内容审核、凭证/计费、请求格式错误——因为 request id 区分的是「上游还是本地」，不是「瞬时还是永久」。「HTTP status 无法判定」的那部分结论现在只计算一次，由两处建立期判定共用，而此前它们各自抄了一份。

真正承重的一半在于错误实际落地的位置。两处建立期判定都只在流建立过程中运行，而 SDK 是在惰性迭代器内部构造这个错误的，此时建立早已 resolve——所以只有流中 catch 会看到它。那个 catch 本来算出了分类结论、随后又忽略了它：它唯一的重试出口要求 socket 错误码。现在它让这一类错误进入既有的两种恢复机制，与传输层那一种并列，用属于自己的判定函数——尚未向调用方交付任何可见内容时走重放，已经交付过文本时走续传——并复用它们的预算与全部「不重复输出」前提。socket 白名单刻意没有改动，因为 Anthropic 生成器共用它来决定延迟的 tool call 分片能否释放。

放宽这道判定又暴露出它自身的顺序缺陷，已在第三轮修复：这道判定在其下方的一次性溢出恢复之前被求值，因此一个无 status 的输入长度拒绝会被原样重发而不是走压缩，而续传一侧每次尝试重发的 payload 都严格更大。现在两个溢出探测器都在判定之上计算，其命中会从放宽后的结论中排除——只从这一类结论中排除，因此 socket 断开保持与本分支存在之前逐字节相同的结论。永久性也不再只读服务端的 `code`，同时读 `.type`，因为 OpenAI SDK 把 `invalid_request_error` 放在 `.type` 上而令 `code` 为 null。三条流恢复日志现在都带上分类的 reason、provider code 与 request id，否则本 PR 所恢复的这一类故障无法从它自己的日志里被定位。

## 为什么需要

一个已经跑了四个多小时的轮次被模型网关的服务端缺陷瞬间终结：流式请求进行到 43 秒时，上游返回 `code: 'KeyError'`、`message: "'id'"`，且没有 HTTP status。同一个会话吸收了几十次 socket 断开而毫无影响，因为那些会被归类为传输层错误并重试；而这种形状一次都没有重试。这个不对称就是缺陷本身——一个由服务端自己用 request id 追踪过的瞬时失败，至少和 socket 断开一样值得重试，但它偏偏是唯一拿不到重试的无 status 形状。用户侧的代价是全额的：整轮中止，错误只显示 `'id'` 两个字符、没有任何上下文，进行中的工作全部丢失。同一模型上 11 小时内复现了三次。

本 PR 的第一个提交并没有真正修好它。它教会了分类器这个形状、放宽了两处建立期判定，而评审查出这两处判定永远看不到该错误：`pipeline.executeStream` 只 await 了响应的创建并返回一个尚未启动的 generator，因此被重试包裹的那次调用在解析任何一个 SSE 帧之前就已 resolve。第二个提交把决策移到错误真正到达的流中 catch。建立期判定保留了，但对这一类而言它们是双保险——本地安装的 SDK 里没有任何生产者会在迭代开始之前构造它。

## 审阅测试计划

### 如何验证

确认以下行为：

1. 上游在流中途推送错误帧且无 HTTP status 时，若尚未向调用方交付任何可见内容，会对同一模型重放；后续尝试成功时该轮正常完成。应看到一个 retry 事件与第二次生成器调用。
2. 同样的失败发生在答案文本已经到达调用方之后时，走续传而不是重放——调用方保留屏幕上已有的内容，模型被要求从那里继续，两半各到达一次且仅一次。这与 socket 断开获得的是同一套恢复。
3. 以同样方式送达的永久性服务端拒绝——诸如 `data_inspection_failed` 的审核码、凭证或计费码、请求格式错误码——仍然在第一次尝试就传播：一次调用、零个 retry 事件。重发同一请求绝不可能成功，而走完整套生产退避阶梯约需八十秒。
4. 本地永久性失败的行为不变。缺少 API key、MCP 服务配置无效、MCP 协议错误（数字 JSON-RPC 码）仍然第一次就失败——它们都不带上游 request id。空 request id 同样不会打开闸门：`x-request-id` 可能存在但为空，那正是上游没有设置该头时代理发出的形状。
5. 带 HTTP status 的上游错误保持原有结论：被追踪的 400 仍然快速失败，5xx 仍然重试，429/503 仍然走限流分支。同时被 request id 追踪过的 socket 断开仍归类为传输层，因此重放、续传与 Anthropic 的延迟 tool call 释放都照常工作。
6. 没有放开任何无界行为。无 status 的上游错误不会进入持久重试模式（仍要求 429 或 529 status）、不会触发模型 fallback（仍要求 status），其流中恢复受既有预算约束——两次重放、三次续传。
7. 以同样方式送达的超大 payload 拒绝——无 status、被追踪、且带着永久名单不认识的错误码——会走到一次性压缩而不是被重放：先出现 COMPRESSED 事件，再是 retry，然后是压缩后的答案。重发无法让请求变小，所以恢复判定不得接管它。
8. 把永久性放在服务端 `.type` 而非 `code` 上的请求格式错误拒绝会快速失败，而同样形状下 `.type` 为 `server_error` 时仍保持可重试。

本次修复对应的真实故障，取自 daemon 日志与会话记录：

```
qwen-code.api_error  error_type="APIError"  error_message="'id'"  status_code=(absent)
                     response_id=cd7f37f3-d38a-9dec-804f-f70dda5650eb  duration_ms=42925
turn_result          state="error"  error={"message":"'id'","code":"KeyError"}
prompt turn failed: [code -32603] 'id'
```

那个裸 UUID 形式的 response id 正是关键线索：该模型成功补全上报的是 `chatcmpl-<uuid>`，所以这个 id 来自错误对象自己的 request id 字段，而不是来自某个补全分片。

本 PR 新增的每一条测试都做过变异验证：移除它所钉住的那处生产改动、确认它变红、再恢复。移除流中那个析取项会让两条流中测试以故障本身的 `'id'` 变红；移除永久错误码名单会让三条变红，其中传播测试报出第二次生成器调用而不是挂死；回退空 id 归一化与 request id 分支，各自的用例分别变红。第三轮新增的用例同样逐一验证：去掉溢出排除项得到 `expected 'retry' to be 'compressed'`；去掉 `.type` 那一项会让请求格式错误用例变红，而把它放宽成「任意 type 都算永久」会让 `server_error` 守卫变红；从永久名单删掉一个错误码会让该码扫描变红；从读取链里去掉 `requestID` 会让真实 SDK oracle 变红；从恢复日志里去掉 `requestId` 会让日志断言变红。

### 前后对比证据

N/A——不涉及 UI 或 TUI 界面变化。可观察的差别是：流中途的网关错误不再中止整轮而是被恢复；上面那段生产日志是 Before，流中测试是 After。

### 测试环境

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### 环境（可选）

仅单元测试，macOS 上执行：全 workspace 构建、全量类型检查、改动文件的格式与 lint 检查，以及重试、分类、流式对话、MCP 客户端、限流识别、OpenAI 内容生成器、Anthropic 生成器、两个非流式 LLM 客户端与聊天压缩各套测试——共 2495 条通过。未调用真实服务端；上游错误形状取自录制的会话，并与本地安装的 SDK 流迭代器逐项对齐。

- 未验证 / 不在范围内：没有集成测试去驱动一个假的 OpenAI SSE 服务端发出流中错误帧，因此 SDK 层的形状是通过阅读本地安装的 SDK 并对齐四个遥测字段来验证的，而不是通过端到端复现执行验证。「过窄」的一侧同样不在范围内：Anthropic 的流中错误会完全丢掉 request id（其 `APIError.generate` 在缺 status/headers 时短路成不带响应头的连接错误），不转发 `x-request-id` 的网关会原样复现原缺陷，藏在 SDK 自身错误体内部的 id 也不会被读取。要从结构上而非响应头识别「无 status 的服务端响应错误」，是一次应当独立成 PR 的设计变更。同样不在范围内：失败文案仍以裸的两字符消息抵达 UI，不带模型或服务端上下文。

无。是在排查一个被中止的会话时发现的，目前没有 issue 跟踪。

issue.body:
## What this PR does

Retries transient 5xx errors received while reading an established model stream, provided no answer text or tool calls have been delivered. These errors share the existing two-retry replay budget with retryable transport failures, with 1-second and 2-second delays. HTTP connection retries and rate-limit retries retain their existing budgets.

## Why it's needed

A Responses stream can establish successfully and then emit a `server_error`, either as an `error` event or through `response.failed`. Although the error is classified as retryable, it occurs outside the HTTP connection retry wrapper and previously terminated the turn immediately. This adds bounded recovery for that failure path while preserving the final provider diagnostic when retries are exhausted.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Point the CLI at a local Responses-compatible SSE endpoint that accepts the request with HTTP 200, emits a transient server error on its first stream, and returns a successful answer on its next request. Confirm the CLI completes successfully after exactly two requests. Then exercise the following cases:

- Confirm flat, nested and `response.failed` server errors recover when the next response succeeds; thinking-only output from an abandoned attempt must not remain in the completed history.
- Confirm repeated server errors stop after three requests and preserve the last error. Mixed server and transport failures must share that same replay budget.
- Confirm cancellation, client errors and errors after delivered text or tool calls do not gain extra retries. HTTP establishment failures, exhausted 503 retries and custom 5xx rate-limit codes must not acquire a second retry budget.

### Evidence (Before & After)

| Scenario | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stream emits `server_error`; next request would succeed | Exits after one request | Second request succeeds |
| Every stream emits `server_error` | Exits after one request | Stops after three requests, preserving the third error |
| Stream emits text or a tool call before the error | No replay | No replay |

On this PR commit, all 569 regression tests and all 9 CLI loopback scenarios passed. Full build, bundle, workspace and integration typechecks, ESLint, and formatting checks passed. The CLI checks verify actual HTTP request counts and final exit status; the tool-boundary case never executed its marker-file tool.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ✅ tested |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested locally |
|  🐧 Linux  | ⚠️ not tested locally |

### Environment (optional)

Node.js 24.18.0 on macOS. CLI checks use the built bundle with isolated configuration/runtime directories, a loopback Responses SSE server and a dummy API key. No live model requests are required.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: transient server failures can now incur up to two additional model requests and three seconds of backoff. Replays remain restricted to attempts without delivered answer text or tool calls.
- Not validated / out of scope: real provider outages and long-running benchmark results; recovery after delivered tool calls; Windows/Linux runtime behavior.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none; no new configuration or public API.

## Linked Issues

No linked issue; found during Responses error-recovery testing.

- 未验证或不在范围内：真实服务商故障、长时间基准评测结果、已交付工具调用后的恢复，以及 Windows/Linux 运行行为。

evidence_units.claim: Issue #7832 reports that large headless/YOLO generations fail when a gateway closes the streaming socket after several minutes. It keeps delivered text, asks the model to resume, and emits `{ RETRY, isContinuation: true }` so the caller keeps its existing text buffer.

On success, the delivered prefix is merged into the trailing model turn, replayed overlap is deduplicated, continuation is bounded to three attempts, and cuts that delivered a function call are excluded because inserting a user turn before its function response would produce an invalid provider sequence.

The pinned change extracts `resetTransportContinuation()` and calls it before the transport replay and reactive compression branches emit a plain non-continuation RETRY. The continuation buffer no longer uses raw accumulation across attempts. The replay gate is made an exact complement of the continuation gate: replay is allowed only when the accumulated continuation buffer is empty, while a retryable cut after any previously delivered text continues even if the current attempt yielded only a thought part or nothing. The old test asserting that a later no-output cut drops continuation is rewritten to assert that the text survives into the next request and history.

The retry event has distinct caller-visible semantics: plain RETRY discards the current streamed output, while the continuation marker preserves the text already shown. The commit explicitly aligns the continuation shape with the existing MAX_TOKENS recovery path and notes that rate-limit and invalid-stream branches already re-send after streamed thought content.

`packages/core/src/core/geminiChat.test.ts` adds branch-specific reset tests, updates the later-cut/no-current-output behavior, and covers delivered-text merge positions involving thought parts. The commit reports the final suite at 277 passing tests in `geminiChat.test.ts`.
